newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHANG POWERS PAST HENMAN TO REACH FOURTH ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG POWERS PAST HENMAN TO REACH FOURTH ROUND.

text.p: American world number two Michael Chang knocked rising British tennis star Tim Henman out of the Australian Open on Friday with a straight-sets win.
Despite occasional flashes of brilliance from the Englishman, Chang beat Henman 6-1 7-6 6-3 on the Melbourne Park centre court to earn a place in the last 16.

Henman last year became the first Briton to reach the men's quarter-finals at Wimbledon for more than 20 years. Last week he ousted world number three Goran Ivanisevic en route to his first tour title in Sydney.
But Chang was consistently a class above Henman, dominating the game from the baseline, lobbing beautifully and moving tirelessly around the court.
Chang, who took one hour 44 minutes to wrap up the match, will next play Andrei Medvedev of Ukraine.
